correctness.rationale: For every r with r/gcd(r,d^n)=m, precisely phi(r)/phi(m) primitive roots map to a fixed primitive alpha. Free Galois action of Gal(KQ(zeta_r)/K), of order phi(r)/[K cap Q(zeta_r):Q], produces exactly [K cap Q(zeta_r):F] factors. Kronecker--Weber and Q(zeta_u) cap Q(zeta_v)=Q(zeta_gcd(u,v)) reduce the degrees to finitely capped valuation coordinates, giving an exact polynomial beyond a concrete conductor threshold and the specified positive leading coefficient. Summing Euler factors derives the cyclotomic all-level product. Exact independent Galois-orbit tests pass for 624 cyclotomic cases, six quadratic cases and five nonstandard targets. The tests support but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 Tucker--Zhu theorem gives the exact minimal-field count and only degree bounds for general number fields. The new statement adds exact intersection-weighted counts at every level, complete invariance under the cyclotomic part of an arbitrary number field, an exact eventual polynomial of specified degree, and the sharp leading coefficient. Its proof genuinely uses additional Galois-orbit and finite-conductor arguments, not an assertion of new root-order parametrization. Related 2017 work studies boundedness and does not state these counts. Residual priority risk: previous implicit applications of standard cyclotomic intersection theory might cover the formula; the original proof makes this extension approachable.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier publication may record the exact cyclotomic intersection sum or its eventual-polynomial specialization.
The result is an accessible elaboration of the root-order argument of Tucker--Zhu, so the separation from prior implicit coverage may be debated.
Exact field-intersection computations for general algebraic input may require separate computational algebra software; the supplied checker validates cyclotomic and two explicit quadratic cases only.

value.rationale: The source paper establishes a new failure of eventual stability and proves only general-field upper/lower factor-count bounds. The new theorem computes the natural full factor-count invariant exactly for every number field, determines its eventual polynomial and sharp leading constant, and explains nonabelian invariance and cross-prime conductor coupling. These are substantive missing quantitative outcomes, not a changed normalization, a small finite cutoff, or a trivial one-parameter table. Scope is explicitly limited to power maps and root-of-unity targets.
